8.1.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.1.text: Arjuna said, "What is Brahman? What is known as the Lord of the Self (Adhyatma)? What is action? O Best of Persons, what is said to be the Lord of material things (Adhibhuta)? What is called the Lord of divinities (Adhidaiva)?"

8.1.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.1.text: Arjuna said, O Supreme Person, what is Brahman? What exists in the individual plane? What is action? What is said to exist in the physical plane? And what is said to exist in the divine plane?

8.1.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.1.text: Arjuna said, O Supreme Person, what is Brahman? What exists in the individual plane? What is action? What is said to exist in the physical plane? And what is said to exist in the divine plane?

8.1.author: Swami Sivananda
8.1.text: Arjuna said, "What is Brahman? What is Adhyatma? What is action, O best among men? What is Adhibhuta declared to be? And, what is Adhidaiva said to be?"

8.1.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.1.text: Arjuna asked: O Lord of Lords! What is that which people call the Supreme Spirit, what is humanity's spiritual nature, and what is the law? What is matter and what is divinity?

8.2.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.2.text: Who is the Lord of Sacrifices, and how? Who is in this body? O slayer of Madhu, how can the self-controlled realize You at the time of their journey (i.e., death)?

8.2.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.2.text: O Madhusudana, how is the entity existing in the sacrifice here in this body, and who is it? And how are You to be known by people of concentrated minds at the time of death?

8.2.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.2.text: O Madhusudana, how is the entity existing in the sacrifice here in this body, and who is it? And how are You to be known by people of concentrated minds at the time of death?

8.2.author: Swami Sivananda
8.2.text: Who and how is Adhiyajna here in this body, O destroyer of Madhu? And how, at the time of death, are You to be known by the self-controlled?

8.2.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.2.text: Who rules the spirit sacrifice in many, and how may those who have learned self-control come to the knowledge of Thee at the time of death?

8.3.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.3.text: The Bhagavat said, "The immutable Absolute is the Brahman. Its intrinsic nature is called the Lord of the Self. The emitting activity that causes the birth of both the animate and inanimate is named 'action'."

8.3.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.3.text: The Blessed Lord said, "The Immutable is the supreme Brahman; selfhood is said to be the entity present in the individual plane. By action is meant the offerings that bring about the origin of existence of things."

8.3.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.3.text: The Blessed Lord said, "The Immutable is the supreme Brahman; selfhood is said to be the entity present in the individual plane. By action is meant the offerings that bring about the origin of existence of things."

8.3.author: Swami Sivananda
8.3.text: The Blessed Lord said, "Brahman is the Imperishable, the Supreme; its essential nature is called Self-knowledge; the offering (to the gods) that causes the existence and manifestation of beings and sustains them is called action."

8.3.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.3.text: The Lord Shri Krishna replied: The Supreme Spirit is the Highest Imperishable Self, and Its nature is spiritual consciousness. The worlds have been created and are sustained by an emanation from the Spirit, which is called the Law.

8.4.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.4.text: The changing nature is the lord of the material beings; the Person alone is the lord of the divinities; I am alone the Lord of sacrifices, and I, the best of the embodied souls, dwell in this body.

8.4.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.4.text: That which exists in the physical plane is the mutable entity, and what exists in the divine plane is the Person. O best among the embodied beings, I Myself am the entity that exists in the sacrifice within this body.

8.4.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.4.text: That which exists in the physical plane is the mutable entity, and what exists in the divine plane is the Person. O best among the embodied beings, I Myself am the entity that exists in the sacrifice within this body.

8.4.author: Swami Sivananda
8.4.text: Adhibhuta—knowledge of the elements—pertains to My perishable nature, and the Purusha, or the Soul, is the Adhidaiva; I alone am the Adhiyajna here in this body, O best among the embodied.

8.4.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.4.text: Matter consists of forms that perish; Divinity is the Supreme Self; and He who inspires the spirit of sacrifice in man, O noblest of their race, is I Myself, Who now stand in human form before thee.

8.5.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.5.text: Whosoever, at the time of death, remembering Me alone, sets forth, abandoning their body behind, they attain My being. There is no doubt about it.

8.5.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.5.text: And at the time of death, anyone who departs, giving up the body while thinking of Me alone, attains My state; there is no doubt about this.

8.5.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.5.text: And at the time of death, anyone who departs, giving up the body while thinking of Me alone, attains My state; there is no doubt about this.

8.5.author: Swami Sivananda
8.5.text: And whoever, leaving their body, goes forth remembering Me alone at the time of death, they will attain My Being; there is no doubt about this.

8.5.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.5.text: Whosoever, at the time of death, thinks only of Me and, thinking thus, leaves the body and goes forth, will assuredly know Me.

8.6.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.6.text: And also remembering whatever being one has been constantly thinking about, a person leaves his body at the end [of his life], O son of Kunti! That being alone he attains.

8.6.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.6.text: O son of Kunti, thinking of any entity, whichever it may be, one gives up the body at the end; he attains that very one, having been always engrossed in its thought.

8.6.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.6.text: O son of Kunti, thinking of any entity, whichever it may be, one gives up the body at the end; he attains that very one, having been always engrossed in its thought.

8.6.author: Swami Sivananda
8.6.text: Whoever at the end leaves the body, thinking of any being, to that being only does he go, O son of Kunti (Arjuna), due to his constant thought of that being.

8.6.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.6.text: Whatever sphere of being the mind of a man is intent on at the time of death, to that he will go.

8.7.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.7.text: Therefore, at all times keep Me in your mind and fight; then, having your mind and intellect dedicated to Me, you will undoubtedly attain Me alone.

8.7.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.7.text: Therefore, think of Me at all times and fight; there is no doubt that by dedicating your mind and intellect to Me, you will attain only Me.

8.7.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.7.text: Therefore, think of Me at all times and fight; there is no doubt that by dedicating your mind and intellect to Me, you will attain only Me.

8.7.author: Swami Sivananda
8.7.text: Therefore, at all times, remember Me only and fight. With your mind and intellect fixed on Me, you will undoubtedly come to Me alone.

8.7.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.7.text: Therefore, always meditate on Me and fight; if your mind and reason are fixed on Me, you will surely come to Me.

8.8.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.8.text: He who is engaged in reflecting on the Supreme Divine Soul with his mind, remaining fixed in the practice of yoga and not focusing on any other object, that person attains the Supreme, O son of Prtha!

8.8.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.8.text: O son of Prtha, by meditating with a mind engaged in the yoga of practice and not straying away to anything else, one reaches the supreme Person existing in the effulgent region.

8.8.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.8.text: O son of Prtha, by meditating with a mind engaged in the yoga of practice and not straying away to anything else, one reaches the supreme Person existing in the effulgent region.

8.8.author: Swami Sivananda
8.8.text: With the mind not moving towards any other thing, made steadfast through the practice of habitual meditation, and constantly meditating, one goes to the Supreme Person, the Resplendent, O Arjuna.

8.8.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.8.text: He whose mind does not wander, and who is engaged in constant meditation, attains the Supreme Spirit.

8.9.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.9.text: He who meditates continuously on the Ancient Seer, the Ruler, the subtler than the subtle, the supporter of all, the unimaginably formed, the sun-colored, and that which is beyond darkness;

8.9.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.9.text: He who meditates on the Omniscient, the Ancient, the Ruler, subtler than the subtle, the Ordainer of everything, of inconceivable form, effulgent like the sun, and beyond darkness—he attains the Supreme Person.

8.9.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.9.text: He who meditates on the Omniscient, the Ancient, the Ruler, subtler than the subtle, the Ordainer of everything, of inconceivable form, effulgent like the sun, and beyond darkness—he attains the Supreme Person.

8.9.author: Swami Sivananda
8.9.text: Whosoever meditates on the Omniscient, the Ancient, the Ruler of the whole world, minuter than an atom, the supporter of all, of inconceivable form, effulgent like the sun and beyond the darkness of ignorance.

8.9.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.9.text: Whoso meditates on the Omniscient, the Ancient, more minute than an atom, yet the Ruler and Upholder of all, Unimaginable, Brilliant like the Sun, Beyond the reach of darkness;

8.10.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.10.text: That person, endowed with a steady mind, devotion, and the power of yoga, reaches the Supreme Divine Soul at the time of departure, by properly fixing the life-breath between their eyebrows.

8.10.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.10.text: At the time of death, having fully fixed the Prana (vital force) between the eyebrows with an unwavering mind, and being imbued with devotion as well as the strength of concentration, he reaches that resplendent Supreme Person.

8.10.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.10.text: At the time of death, having fully fixed the Prana (vital force) between the eyebrows with an unwavering mind, and being imbued with devotion as well as the strength of concentration, he reaches that resplendent Supreme Person.

8.10.author: Swami Sivananda
8.10.text: At the time of death, with an unwavering mind, endowed with devotion, by the power of Yoga, fixing the whole life-breath in the middle of the two eyebrows, he reaches that resplendent Supreme Person.

8.10.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.10.text: He who leaves the body with an unmoved mind, filled with devotion, and by the power of his meditation gathers his whole vital energy between his eyebrows, attains the Supreme.

8.11.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.11.text: That Unchanging One which the Vedic knowers speak of; which the passion-free ascetics enter into, seeking which they practice celibacy (or spiritual life); that Goal together with the means [to reach it] I shall tell you.

8.11.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.11.text: I will briefly speak to you of that immutable Goal, which the knowers of the Vedas declare; into which diligent ones, free from attachment, enter, and for which people practice celibacy, aspiring.

8.11.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.11.text: I will briefly tell you about that immutable Goal which the knowers of the Vedas declare; those who are diligent, free from attachment, and aspire for it, enter into it. People practice celibacy for it.

8.11.author: Swami Sivananda
8.11.text: That which is declared to be Imperishable by those who know the Vedas, that which the self-controlled (ascetics or Sannyasins) and passion-free enter, that goal, desiring which celibacy is practised, I will declare to thee in brief.

8.11.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.11.text: Now, I will briefly speak of the imperishable goal, proclaimed by those who are versed in the scriptures, which the mystic attains when free from passion, and for which they are content to undergo the vow of continence.

8.12.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.12.text: Properly controlling all the gates of the body; restraining the mind firmly in the heat; fixing one's own prana in the head; taking refuge in the firmness of Yoga.

8.12.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.12.text: Having controlled all the senses, confined the mind in the heart, and fixed his own vital force in the head, he should remain steadfast in yoga.

8.12.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.12.text: Having controlled all the senses, confined the mind in the heart, and fixed his own vital force in the head, he should remain firm in yoga.

8.12.author: Swami Sivananda
8.12.text: Having closed all the gates, confined the mind in the heart, and fixed the life-breath in the head, engage in the practice of concentration.

8.12.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.12.text: Closing the gates of the body, drawing the forces of his mind into the heart, and, by the power of meditation, concentrating his vital energy in the brain;

8.13.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.13.text: Reciting the single-syllabled Om, the very Brahman; meditating on Me; whoever travels well, casting away their body—surely they attain My State.

8.13.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.13.text: He who departs, leaving the body while uttering the single syllable, viz. "Om," which is Brahman, and thinking of Me, attains the supreme Goal.

8.13.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.13.text: He who departs, leaving the body while uttering the single syllable, "Om," which is Brahman, and thinking of Me, attains the supreme Goal.

8.13.author: Swami Sivananda
8.13.text: Uttering the one-syllabled Om, the Brahman, and remembering Me, he who departs, leaving the body, attains the Supreme Goal.

8.13.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.13.text: Repeating Om, the symbol of eternity, and holding Me always in remembrance, he who thus leaves his body and goes forth reaches the Supreme Spirit.

8.14.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.14.text: And whoever constantly bears Me in mind, never attached to any other object—for this yogi, ever devoted, I am easy to attain, O son of Prtha!

8.14.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.14.text: O son of Prtha, to that yogi of constant concentration and single-minded attention, who remembers Me uninterruptedly and for a long time, I am easy to attain.

8.14.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.14.text: O son of Prtha, to that yogi of constant concentration and single-minded attention, who remembers Me uninterruptedly and for a long time, I am easily attained.

8.14.author: Swami Sivananda
8.14.text: I am easily attainable by that ever-steadfast yogi who constantly and daily remembers me for a long time, not thinking of anything else with a single-minded or one-pointed focus, O Partha.

8.14.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.14.text: To him who constantly thinks of Me and nothing else, to such an ever-faithful devotee, O Arjuna, I am ever accessible.

8.15.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.15.text: Having attained Me, the men of great soul who have achieved the supreme perfection do not get the transient birth, a storehouse of all troubles.

8.15.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.15.text: As a result of reaching Me, the exalted ones who have attained the highest perfection do not get birth, which is an abode of sorrows and is impermanent.

8.15.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.15.text: As a result of reaching Me, the exalted ones who have attained the highest perfection do not get rebirth, which is an abode of sorrows and is impermanent.

8.15.author: Swami Sivananda
8.15.text: Having attained Me, these great souls do not take birth again here—a place of pain and impermanence—but have reached the highest perfection of liberation.

8.15.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.15.text: Coming to Me in this way, these great souls no longer go to the misery and death of earthly life, for they have achieved perfection.

8.16.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.16.text: Till the Brahman is attained, people return from each and every world, O Arjuna! But there is no return for one who has attained Me, O son of Kunti!

8.16.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.16.text: O Arjuna, all the worlds together with the world of Brahma are subject to return. But, O son of Kunti, there is no rebirth after reaching Me.

8.16.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.16.text: O Arjuna, all the worlds together with the world of Brahma are subject to return. But, O son of Kunti, there is no return after reaching Me.

8.16.author: Swami Sivananda
8.16.text: All the worlds, including the world of Brahma, are subject to return again, O Arjuna; but he who reaches Me, O son of Kunti, has no rebirth.

8.16.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.16.text: The worlds, along with the entire realm of creation, come and go; but, O Arjuna, whoever comes to Me, for them there is no rebirth.

8.17.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.17.text: Those who know the day of Brahma as encompassing one thousand yugas (world-ages), and night [also] as encompassing one thousand yugas—those people know the day and night of Brahma.

8.17.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.17.text: Those people who know what day and night are, know the day of Brahma which ends in a thousand yugas [The four yugas (in the human worlds), viz Satya, Treta, Dwapara, and Kali are made up of 4,320,000 years. This period multiplied by a thousand constitutes one day of Brahma. His night also extends over a similar period. See M.S. and V.S.A.], and His night which also ends in a thousand yugas.

8.17.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.17.text: Those people who know what day and night are, know the day of Brahma which ends in a thousand yugas, and His night which also ends in a thousand yugas.

8.17.author: Swami Sivananda
8.17.text: Those who know the day of Brahma, which lasts a thousand Yugas, and the night, which also lasts a thousand Yugas, know day and night.

8.17.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.17.text: Those who understand the cosmic day and night know that one day of creation is a thousand cycles, and that the night is of equal length.

8.18.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.18.text: As the day approaches, all manifestations emerge from the unmanifest, and as the night approaches, they dissolve into the same, which is known as the 'unmanifest.'

8.18.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.18.text: With the coming of day, all manifested things emerge from the Unmanifest, and when night comes, they merge into that which is called the Unmanifested.

8.18.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.18.text: With the coming of day, all manifested things emerge from the Unmanifest, and when night comes, they merge into that which is called the Unmanifested.

8.18.author: Swami Sivananda
8.18.text: From the Unmanifested, all the manifested worlds proceed upon the arrival of the 'day'; upon the arrival of the 'night', they dissolve indeed into that which is known as the Unmanifested.

8.18.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.18.text: At the dawn of that day, all objects in manifestation stream forth from the Unmanifest, and when evening falls, they are dissolved back into it again.

8.19.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.19.text: Being born and reborn, the same multitude of beings is dissolved when night approaches and is born again, willy-nilly, when day approaches, O son of Prtha!

8.19.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.19.text: O son of Prtha, after being born again and again, that very multitude of beings disappears of its own accord at the approach of night. It comes to life again at the approach of day.

8.19.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.19.text: O son of Prtha, after being born again and again, that very multitude of beings disappears of its own accord at the approach of night. It comes to life again at the approach of day.

8.19.author: Swami Sivananda
8.19.text: This same multitude of beings, being born again and again, helplessly dissolves, O Arjuna, into the Unmanifested at the coming of the night and comes forth at the coming of the day.

8.19.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.19.text: The same multitude of beings, which have lived on earth so often, all are dissolved as the night of the universe approaches, to issue forth anew when morning breaks. Thus, it is ordained.

8.20.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.20.text: But there exists another Being which is beyond this, and It is both manifest and unmanifest and is eternal. It is this Being that does not perish while all other beings perish.

8.20.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.20.text: But distinct from that Unmanifested is the other eternal, unmanifest Reality, who does not get destroyed when all beings are destroyed.

8.20.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.20.text: But distinct from that Unmanifested is the other eternal, unmanifest Reality, who does not get destroyed when all beings are destroyed.

8.20.author: Swami Sivananda
8.20.text: But verily, there exists higher than this Unmanifested, another Unmanifested Eternal, which is not destroyed even when all beings are destroyed.

8.20.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.20.text: In truth, therefore, there is the eternal, unmanifest, which is beyond and above the unmanifest spirit of creation, and which is never destroyed when all these beings perish.

8.21.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.21.text: The scriptures speak of This as Unmanifest and Changeless, and declare This to be the highest Goal. Having attained it, people do not return; this is My highest abode.

8.21.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.21.text: They call Him who has been mentioned as the Unmanifested, the Immutable, the supreme Goal. That is the supreme abode of Mine, from which they do not return once they reach it.

8.21.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.21.text: They call Him who has been mentioned as the Unmanifested, the Immutable, the supreme Goal. That is the supreme abode of Mine, from which they do not return once they reach it.

8.21.author: Swami Sivananda
8.21.text: What is known as the Unmanifested and the Imperishable, That is said to be the highest goal. Those who reach It do not return (to this Samsara). That is My supreme abode (place or state).

8.21.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.21.text: The wise say that the Unmanifest and Indestructible is the highest goal of all; when once that is reached, there is no returning. That is my blessed home.

8.22.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.22.text: O son of Prtha, the Supreme Soul is attainable through devotion that admits no other things; having attained it, the men of Yoga do not get birth again; within it exist the beings, and everything is well established in it, O Arjuna!

8.22.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.22.text: O son of Prtha, that supreme Person—in whom all beings are included and by whom all this is pervaded—is indeed reached through one-pointed devotion.

8.22.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.22.text: O son of Prtha, that supreme Person—in whom all beings are included and by whom all this is pervaded—is, indeed, reached through one-pointed devotion.

8.22.author: Swami Sivananda
8.22.text: That highest Purusha, O Arjuna, is attainable by unswerving devotion to Him alone, within Whom all beings dwell and by Whom all this is pervaded.

8.22.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.22.text: O Arjuna! That Highest God, in Whom all beings abide, and Who pervades the entire universe, is reached only by wholehearted devotion. *He is the one who determines the course of worldly events and the destiny of all living beings.*

8.23.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.23.text: Departing at what times the Yogis attain the non-return or the return only—those times I shall declare to you, O chief of the Bharatas!

8.23.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.23.text: O best of the Bharata dynasty, I shall now speak of that time by which the yogis depart and attain the State of Non-return, and also the State of Return.

8.23.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.23.text: O best of the Bharata dynasty, I shall now speak of that time by which the yogis depart and attain the State of Non-return, and also the State of Return.

8.23.author: Swami Sivananda
8.23.text: Now I will tell you, O chief of the Bharatas, the times of departure at which the Yogis will return or not return.

8.23.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.23.text: Now, I will tell you, O Arjuna, the times at which, if the mystics go forth, they do not return, and at which they go forth only to return.

8.24.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.24.text: The northern course consisting of six months is fire, light, day, and bright. Departing in it, the Brahman-knowing men attain Brahman.

8.24.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.24.text: Fire, light, daytime, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern solstice—by following this path, persons who are knowers of Brahman attain Brahman when they die.

8.24.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.24.text: Fire, light, daytime, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern solstice—by following this path, persons who are knowers of Brahman attain Brahman when they die.

8.24.author: Swami Sivananda
8.24.text: Fire, light, daytime, the bright fortnight, the six months of the northern path of the sun (the northern solstice) departing, then men who know Brahman go to Brahman.

8.24.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.24.text: If the sage, knowing the Supreme Spirit, goes forth with fire and light during the day, in the fortnight of the waxing moon, and in the six months before the Northern summer solstice, he will attain the Supreme.

8.25.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.25.text: The southern course of the sun, consisting of six months, is smoke, night, and darkness. Departing in it, the yogi attains the light of the moon and returns.

8.25.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.25.text: Following this Path, the yogi, having reached the lunar light, returns, smoke, night, as also the dark fortnight and the six months of the Southern solstice.

8.25.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.25.text: Following this Path, the yogi, having reached the lunar light, returns, smoke, night, as also the dark fortnight and the six months of the Southern solstice.

8.25.author: Swami Sivananda
8.25.text: Attaining the lunar light through smoke, night time, the dark fortnight, and the six months of the southern path of the sun (the southern solstice), the yogi returns.

8.25.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.25.text: But if he departs in gloom, at night, during the fortnight of the waning moon and in the six months before the winter solstice, then he reaches only lunar light and he will be reborn.

8.26.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.26.text: For, these two bright and dark paths are considered to be perpetual for the world. One attains non-return by the first of these, and one returns back by the other.

8.26.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.26.text: These two paths of the world, which are white and black, are indeed considered eternal. Through one, a person goes to the state of non-return; through the other, they return again.

8.26.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.26.text: These two paths of the world, which are white and black, are indeed considered eternal. Through one, a person goes to the state of non-return; through the other, they return again.

8.26.author: Swami Sivananda
8.26.text: The bright and dark paths of the world are thought to be eternal; one leads to no return, and the other leads to return.

8.26.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.26.text: These bright and dark paths out of the world have always existed. Whoever takes the former, does not return; he who chooses the latter, returns.

8.27.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.27.text: O son of Prtha, no Yogin, knowing these two courses, gets deluded. Therefore, O Arjuna, practice Yoga connected with all times.

8.27.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.27.text: O son of Prtha, no yogi—one steadfast in meditation—whosoever has known these two courses becomes deluded. Therefore, O Arjuna, be steadfast in yoga at all times.

8.27.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.27.text: O son of Prtha, no yogi—one steadfast in meditation—whosoever has known these two courses becomes deluded. Therefore, O Arjuna, be steadfast in yoga at all times.

8.27.author: Swami Sivananda
8.27.text: Knowing these paths, O Arjuna, no yogi is deluded; therefore, at all times, be steadfast in yoga.

8.27.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.27.text: O Arjuna! The saint, knowing these paths, is not confused; therefore, meditate perpetually.

8.28.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
8.28.text: Having understood all this, the Yogin goes beyond whatever fruit of merit is ordained in the scriptures in case of reciting the Vedas, performing sacrifices, observing austerities, and donating gifts; and he goes to the Supreme Primeval Abode.

8.28.author: Swami Adidevananda
8.28.text: Having known this, the yogi transcends all the results of righteous deeds declared in the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities, and charities, and reaches the primordial, supreme state.

8.28.author: Swami Gambirananda
8.28.text: Having known this, the yogi transcends all the results of righteous deeds declared in the Vedas, sacrifices, austerities, and charities, and reaches the primordial, supreme state.

8.28.author: Swami Sivananda
8.28.text: Whatever fruit of merit is declared (in the scriptures) to accrue from (the study of) the Vedas, (the performance of) sacrifices, (the practice of) austerities, and gifts, beyond all this goes the Yogi, having known this; and he attains to the Supreme, Primeval (first or ancient) Abode.

8.28.author: Shri Purohit Swami
8.28.text: The sage who knows this passes beyond all merit that comes from the study of the scriptures, from sacrifice, from austerities, and from charity, and reaches the Supreme Primeval Abode.
